acceptance: dsdgen, dbgen, dsqgen, qgen and tool compilation are ended at the user's limit and have no limit of BenchBox's own.
Data left by a stopped generator is never reused, on any reuse path, for TPC and non-TPC benchmarks.
Generated data and its hashes are unchanged.

description:
## Problem
BenchBox stops valid generation work with limits of its own, and has no way to stop generation at a user's limit. Read on develop: dsqgen 30 s per query (core/tpcds/c_tools.py) and 300 s per stream set (core/tpcds/streams.py); qgen 10 s (core/tpch/queries.py:66-74); compiling the TPC tools 300 s and 600 s (utils/tpc_compilation.py:481-486, 526-531). dsdgen and dbgen have no limit: core/tpcds/generator/runner.py and streaming.py, core/tpch/generator.py, core/tpch/streams.py, core/tpch/refresh.py:110. Several of these run in thread pools. A generator killed partway can leave data a later run accepts: `DataValidator.validate_data_directory` (utils/data_validation.py:122-200) accepts row counts within 5%, never treats a zero count as a mismatch, and writes a manifest from the scan; the TPC-H generator then reuses the data (core/tpch/generator.py:655-673); for non-TPC benchmarks the check is only that files exist and are non-empty.

## Owner decisions
"We MUST NOT enforce a default timeout." "Why would query generation hit a timeout? That seems insane". Fixed limits: "remove the qgen and compile limits (both then follow `--timeout` only). Keep the 5 and 15 second probes: they run `-h` on a binary to see whether it starts at all, which is a health check, not generation." Partial data: "Data generated by a stopped generator is not marked complete and is not reused." Source: owner's answer in the choice dialog, 2026-11-20.

## Change
1. Every generator and compiler child process on the run path is started through the deadline: it gets the remaining time and is ended with its process group when it runs out (direct child only on Windows). Sites: the ones listed above. Classes capture the deadline in the calling thread so pool threads see it. Confirm by search that no other benchmark under benchbox/core shells out on the run path (the review found none; core/tpcds/qualification/runner.py is not on it).
2. Remove the dsqgen 30 s and 300 s, qgen 10 s and compile 300 s and 600 s limits. Keep the `-h` probes (tpch/generator.py:278-282, tpc_compilation.py:311-316). Reword the dsqgen error that names a 30-second limit.
3. One process-group helper in `benchbox/utils` that sends TERM, waits, then KILL: move the one in tests/uat/timeouts.py:126-170 into the package and have UAT import it. (Step 5 then only deletes the remaining duplicates.)
4. An in-progress marker file written in the data directory before a generator starts and removed only when it finishes successfully. Every reuse path refuses data while the marker is present and regenerates: the manifest path (core/runner/runner.py), the scan path (data_validation.py) and the TPC-H generator's own reuse. Cover TPC-DS, TPC-H and one non-TPC benchmark.

## Decision gates
A limit, default, threshold, status token, message or label text the owner has chosen is used verbatim (see run-timeout-plan-20261120). Any other new name or message follows existing BenchBox conventions and is listed in the pull request (owner, 2026-11-21: no stop for these). The marker's file name is internal and is stated in the pull request body. No change to what data is generated or to any digest; show that the data-generation hashes for TPC-H and TPC-DS at SF 0.01 are unchanged. With no deadline set, each call site behaves as before except that the removed fixed limits no longer apply. Do not change execution-phase code here.

## Verification rubric
Pass, each by a test that fails before the change:
- With nothing set, a stubbed dsqgen that outlives 30 s and 300 s, a stubbed qgen that outlives 10 s and a stubbed compile that outlives 600 s are not stopped.
- With a deadline, stubbed dsdgen (single, parallel and streaming paths), dbgen (including refresh-set generation), dsqgen (single and stream), qgen and a compile are each ended at the remaining time, and the error names the user's limit, the tool, and for query generation the query and scale. The parallel test shows a pool thread sees the deadline.
- The `-h` probes still have their limits.
- Partial data: a directory left by a generator killed after writing at least 96% of a table's expected rows, with no manifest, is regenerated on the next run; the same for a directory with a manifest but with the in-progress marker; the same for one non-TPC benchmark. A completed generation leaves no marker and is reused.
- The strings for the removed limits are gone from the modules.
- TPC-H and TPC-DS SF 0.01 data-generation hashes equal develop's.
Also one real check through `make heavy-run`: `benchbox datagen --benchmark tpcds --scale 1 --timeout 2` exits 124, leaves the marker, and a following run without `--timeout` regenerates and completes. `make pr-preflight` exits 0.

## Guardrails (owner, 2026-11-20)
The agent never posts a stand-in review, closes and reopens a pull request to restart CI, uses `--no-verify`, force-pushes, rewrites an author, or deletes anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. Arming: `make pr-arm` once; one more attempt only when the refusal named a cause, the agent reported it and the cause is cleared; never a third without asking; `make pr-rerun` at most once and only for a job that never ran or was cancelled by the runner, never for a test that failed. Review threads: reply, and resolve only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise the finding again. Subagents implement batch members and serial items under the delivery plan on run-timeout-plan-20261120 (owner, 2026-11-21); a batch member makes no tracker write, opens no pull request and stops at a landing report. A limit, default, threshold, status token, message or label text the owner has chosen is used verbatim (see run-timeout-plan-20261120). Any other new name or message follows existing BenchBox conventions and is listed in the pull request (owner, 2026-11-21: no stop for these). No file edit by script; use the edit tool. Do not edit a pull request description while its CI is starting; post a comment. A blocked step stops this item; no workaround. No live cloud run. Heavy work only through `make heavy-run`.
